newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-ELLIOTT FAILS ON RETURN FROM INJURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ELLIOTT FAILS ON RETURN FROM INJURY.

text.p: Victoria opener Matthew Elliott's celebrations at being selected for the South African tour were dampened when he was dismissed cheaply in the Sheffield Shield on Thursday in his first innings after returning from injury.
Elliott, who injured his knee while batting in the second test against West Indies eight weeks ago, made only two as New South Wales dominated the first day of the match in Melbourne.
New South Wales were earlier dismissed for 290 after opener Michael Slater, who lost out to Elliott in the battle for tour selection, laid the foundation for the innings with a typically robust 71.
At close of play on the first day, Victoria were 12 for one wicket.
In Brisbane, Sheffield Shield leaders Western Australia gained the upper hand against their nearest rivals Queensland.
At close of play, the visitors were 102 for four after dismissing Queensland for 179 at the Gabba.
Western Australia opener Mike Hussey scored 15 before being dismissed hit wicket in extraordinary circumstances.
The left-hander attempted a drive through mid-wicket only to lose grip of his bat, which flew over his head before falling onto the stumps behind him.
Western Australia lead the table on 26 points, six points clear of Queensland and New South Wales.
